mewing.text: Users practise mewing in the hope of a more defined jawline, forward midface and better profile, drawing on the orthotropics ideas of John and Mike Mew. The claim that tongue posture reshapes adult facial bone rests on anecdote and before-and-after photos rather than controlled studies.

hard-mewing.text: Hard mewing is a forceful version of tongue posture that forum users adopt for faster jaw and midface change, sometimes alongside thumb pulling and expanders. Some posters report masseter growth, which would be a muscle effect; the bone-change claim is untested and rests on anecdote.

thumb-pulling.text: Users pull on the palate with a thumb as a free stand-in for professional palatal expansion, hoping for a wider palate and more forward midface. It is usually paired with mewing and chewing, and the appearance claim rests on forum anecdote rather than studies.

chewing-for-jaw.text: Users chew mastic gum or tough foods to build the masseters and give the lower face a more defined look, often alongside mewing and neck work. Masseter enlargement from chewing is documented in muscle research; changes to jaw bone from chewing are untested.

facial-yoga-face-exercises.text: Face exercises are promoted as a natural facelift, with users aiming at firmer cheeks, a sharper jawline and a more lifted look around the eyes and mouth. The sources available include no study measuring appearance outcomes, so the claim rests on practitioner and forum accounts.

wolff-s-law-facial-loading.text: Wolff's law, a real principle of bone adaptation, is cited in looksmaxxing circles as the theory behind mewing, chewing and pulling practices that aim to reshape the face. Applying it to adult facial bone through tongue posture or chewing is a theory that has not been tested.

orbital-rubbing-eye-socket-massage.text: Users press or rub around the eye socket in the hope of changing orbit shape and giving the eyes a more open, defined look. It is discussed as a non-surgical option for eye-area aesthetics; no study supports bone change from massage, so the claim rests on anecdote.

nose-bone-massaging-nasal-bone-pushing.text: Users press or massage the nose, usually the bridge, hoping to narrow or reshape it without surgery. It is discussed as a free alternative to rhinoplasty; no study tests it for reshaping, and the medical literature on nasal bones concerns fractures.

hyoid-neck-posture-meta.text: Users discuss raising the hyoid and correcting neck posture, together with reducing submental fat, to sharpen the angle between chin and neck. Chin tucks and neck exercises are the usual tools. The sources available address airway anatomy rather than appearance, so the link rests on forum theory.

palate-expanders-adult.text: Adults use MARPE or surgically assisted expansion, real orthodontic procedures, with the aim of a wider upper jaw and fuller midface and smile. Expansion is studied for transverse jaw deficiency and breathing; its effect on overall facial appearance is untested.

chain: Claimed better jaw and midface development
nasal-breathing-meta.text: Users favour nasal breathing, sometimes with mouth taping, in the belief it supports jaw and midface structure and a leaner face. Studies in children link mouth breathing to growth changes; whether switching as an adult changes appearance is untested.

sleeping-position-for-face-symmetry.text: Users sleep on their back in the belief that it avoids pressing one side of the face into a pillow and keeps the face symmetrical. No study links sleep posture to facial symmetry, so the idea rests on forum anecdote.

cortisol-face-stress-face-claims.text: Forum posters attribute a rounded, puffy or tired-looking face to stress and high cortisol, and aim to lower stress for a leaner look. Facial rounding is documented in medicine with sustained hormone excess; everyday stress has not been tested for this effect.

limb-lengthening-surgery-ll.text: Users pursue limb lengthening to add permanent height, since cutting and slowly extending the femurs or tibias increases leg length, a measurable change. The technique is established in medicine for limb discrepancy and deformity and is also performed electively for cosmetic height gain.

cosmetic-leg-lengthening-precice-nails.text: The Precice nail is a magnetically lengthened internal implant that lets people gain height without an external frame, and the added stature is measurable. It is well studied for medical limb lengthening, with limited data specific to cosmetic use.

hgh-for-height.text: People discuss growth hormone to gain height, either as teenagers or past puberty. It is studied in children with short stature, with modest gains; use in healthy adults with closed growth plates for height is untested.

letrozole-aromatase-inhibitors-for-heigh.text: Teenagers and parents discuss aromatase inhibitors as a way to slow bone maturation and extend growth for extra height. They have been trialled in boys with short stature; their use for height in healthy people is off-label and has no published evidence.

hanging-stretching-for-height.text: Users hang from bars and stretch to decompress the spine and recover or hold height. Brief increases in spinal length are reported after decompression; a lasting gain in adult height has not been tested.

height-increasing-supplements.text: Teenagers and adults ask about vitamin, mineral and herbal blends sold to help them grow taller or reach their genetic potential. Adequate nutrition supports normal growth in childhood; no trial backs these products for adding height in adults.

squatmaxxing-spinal-loading.text: Users squat heavily to build legs and improve physique proportions, and some wonder whether it changes how tall they look. Leg development from squatting is well established as muscle growth; no source ties squatting to a gain in height.

raw-milk-for-height.text: Some height-focused communities drink unpasteurised milk in the belief it promotes growth, with proponents citing nutrition and immunity. No height studies of raw milk exist, so the link rests on anecdote.

height-stretching-devices-inversion.text: Users hang from inversion tables or gravity boots to decompress the spine and add measurable morning height, with some forum posters reporting about two inches. Reported gains are millimetres and short-lived in the available sources.

chain: Correct pelvic tilt and rib flare
posture-for-height-rib-pelvic-tilt.text: Forum users correct anterior pelvic tilt and rib flare to stand taller and look more upright, and some ask whether it also improves facial symmetry. Standing straighter changes how tall someone measures and appears; no study measures stature change from these fixes.

growth-plate-peptides-igf-1-mk-677-for-h.text: Teenagers discuss MK-677 and IGF-1 products as a way to gain height by raising growth hormone signalling. Trials exist in children with growth hormone deficiency; none test healthy short people, so the height use is off-label and rests on anecdote.

manlet-height-tiers.text: Manlet and height tiers are community slang for short men and the brackets used to rank them, and they frame why many users pursue height gains, lifts and better presentation. It is a vocabulary of social hierarchy rather than a method with its own evidence.

anabolic-steroid-stacks-looksmaxxing.text: Forum users discuss steroid combinations for muscle size and a masculine look, including a wider jaw and neck. Muscle gain from anabolic steroids is well documented; claims about facial bone and skeletal width are untested.

short-steroid-cycles-myth.text: Users discuss brief steroid courses as a way to gain muscle while limiting lasting effects on the body's hormones. No trial has tested the idea for appearance use, and medical sources describe hormone recovery as variable.

chain: Claimed facial bone and muscle change
trt-testosterone-for-jaw.text: Users discuss testosterone therapy or related androgens in the hope of a more masculine jaw, midface and neck. Testosterone therapy is established medicine for low testosterone and masculinising treatment; no study tests it for jaw structure in the way looksmaxxers describe.

dht-androgel-for-facial-structure.text: Forum users discuss DHT or testosterone gel during puberty to masculinise facial structure and boost beard growth. Gels are studied for low testosterone in older men; their effect on facial bone development is untested and rests on anecdote.

pentastack.text: The pentastack is a mix of Adderall, dextromethorphan, pregabalin, ketamine and BDO that drew attention in 2026 through looksmaxxing influencers, who describe it as a way to feel more composed in public. It is a news event rather than an appearance method, with no studied link to looks.
